# Locator Source Strategy

Item 2.1 names three genuinely different ways to identify locators. This
project uses all three - none is disabled - but they are not
interchangeable defaults; pick in this order, per the team's recommendation
on the 'Locator Options Comparison' tab.

## Decision order

1. **Option 3 - HTML/repo access (primary, when available).** Check
   `autopilot-ui/configs/new/config.json` for an `htmlSourcePath` (a DevGit
   checkout or a directory of periodic HTML exports). If it's set and the
   path exists, run `npm run extract-html -- <page>.html` and use its
   output (`src/utils/htmlRepoLocatorExtractor.ts`). This is the most
   stable, deterministic source - static, versioned HTML rather than
   something inferred at runtime - and the option most likely to reach the
   ~70% out-of-the-box target. It also speeds up the item 3.1 RCA work,
   since the same access lets the team compare expected vs. actual page
   structure.
2. **Option 1 - Crawling (working fallback).** If no `htmlSourcePath` is
   configured, or the configured path doesn't exist yet (access still
   pending), fall back to `npm run crawl -- <route>` against the live
   application (`src/utils/crawlOnce.ts`). This works today with no new
   access needed. Known gap: it misses shadow-DOM elements and
   popup/dynamic content - flag anything you suspect falls in that category
   rather than silently guessing.
3. **Option 2 - MCP (parallel exploration, not the default path).** Use the
   Playwright MCP server's `browser_snapshot` / `browser_generate_locator`
   tools when you specifically need to inspect *live, rendered* DOM state
   that neither a static export nor a plain crawl would show - for example,
   an element that only appears after a client-side interaction. As of the
   last evaluation on the comparison tab, the team found this "not
   efficient" as a default locator-discovery mechanism, so don't reach for
   it first; use it as a targeted tool for cases 1 and 2 can't resolve, and
   log when you had to.

## Regardless of source

All three paths converge on the same `CandidateLocator` shape
(`src/utils/locatorCandidate.ts`) and the same element-classification logic,
so downstream steps (validation, the `locator-naming-convention` skill,
`output/objects-collections/pageobjects.json`) don't need to know which
option produced a given entry.

Every candidate - from any of the three sources - is still **unvalidated**
until a human or this agent confirms it against the live rendered page. "It
came from static HTML" is not the same guarantee as "it was verified against
the running app." Say which source produced each locator when you report
back, so a reviewer knows how much extra scrutiny it needs.

## Recording the decision

When you resolve locators for a DSL file, note in your chat reply (and in
the sibling `.dsl.notes.md` file per the dsl-governance skill) which option
you used and why - "used Option 1 because `htmlSourcePath` wasn't set" is
exactly the kind of trace the team needs while Option 3 access is still
pending with Cisco IT/Security.

## Learned patterns

Read [references/learned-patterns.md](./references/learned-patterns.md) when choosing or changing a locator. It holds locator edits engineers made by hand: stable-strategy upgrades, fallbacks for unstable elements, scoped locators - fixes that recurred across several files and engineers and were approved by a reviewer (generated by `npm run learn-publish`; do not edit it by hand). Treat it as part of this skill.

If you hit a problem it does not cover, run `npm run lookup-fix -- "<problem>"`. After you fix it by hand, record the fix with `npm run learn-capture -- --worktree --write --why "<what was wrong>"` so it can become a pattern (see the **fix-knowledge-base** skill).
